rules.title: UK 0.1% Direct-to-Consumer Hydrogen Peroxide Limit
rules.expected_requirement: Maximum 0.1% w/w hydrogen peroxide in consumer cosmetic/whitening products.
rules.explanation: Post-Brexit UK retained the EU Annex III limit. Products exceeding 0.1% cannot be sold OTC to UK consumers without a dentist's prescription.
rules.fix_suggestion: Formulate with <= 0.1% hydrogen peroxide or non-peroxide alternative whitening formulations.

rules.statute_citation: UK Product Safety and Metrology Regulations 2019 / SCPN Portal
rules.title: Mandatory UK-Established Responsible Person (GB Address)
rules.expected_requirement: Name and Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales) physical address of the UK Responsible Person.
rules.explanation: Following Brexit, an EU Responsible Person address is no longer valid in the UK. Products must have a UK RP and be notified on the Submit Cosmetic Product Notifications (SCPN) portal prior to marketing.
rules.fix_suggestion: Appoint a UK-based Responsible Person and print their GB address on packaging.

rules.statute_citation: CAP Code Rule 12.1 / MHRA Borderline Guidance Note 8
rules.title: Medicinal Claim Prohibition for Non-Medicinal Products
rules.expected_requirement: Claims must not aver or imply prevention, treatment, or cure of human disease unless holding an MHRA Marketing Authorisation.
rules.explanation: The MHRA rigorously enforces Borderline Note 8. Claims to cure arthritis or eliminate joint pain will trigger Trading Standards seizures and ASA advertising bans.
rules.fix_suggestion: Replace medicinal wording with descriptive lifestyle phrasing: 'designed for soothing massage and muscle relaxation'.

rules.statute_citation: BS EN 1273:2020 / UK General Product Safety Regulations 2005
rules.title: UK Safety Standard for Baby Walkers (BS EN 1273 Check)
rules.expected_requirement: Technical file and test certificate demonstrating compliance with British Standard BS EN 1273:2020.
rules.explanation: Baby walkers are fully lawful in the UK if they pass BS EN 1273 stair safety testing. Testing documentation must be verified.
rules.fix_suggestion: Provide test certificate from a UKAS-accredited laboratory confirming BS EN 1273 compliance.

rules.statute_citation: GB Biocidal Products Regulation (GB BPR) / HSE Guidance
rules.title: UK Classification of Antimicrobial Treated Articles
rules.expected_requirement: Treated article claim permitted if active substance is on GB Article 95 approved list; requires active substance name on label.
rules.explanation: In the UK, cutting boards with antimicrobial properties are regulated as 'treated articles' under GB BPR, NOT as pesticides. While lawful, the label must name the active substance.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure active antimicrobial substance is listed on the UK Article 95 approved list and declare its chemical name on the pack.
